html:
The Temple of Concordia is a Doric temple at Akragas, now Agrigento, on the south coast of Sicily, built around 440 to 430 BCE. It is the largest and best preserved Doric temple in Sicily, and one of the best preserved Greek temples in the world.

Akragas was one of the richest Greek cities in the west. After its ruler Theron helped Syracuse defeat Carthage at the Battle of Himera in 480 BCE, the city used its wealth, and its prisoners of war, to build a row of great temples along a ridge, now called the Valley of the Temples. Carthage sacked Akragas in 406 BCE.

No one knows which god the temple honoured. Its name comes from a Latin inscription found nearby that has nothing to do with it. It survived almost whole because in the late 6th century CE a bishop turned it into a church, cutting arches into the inner walls. It was restored to its Greek form in the 18th century.
